create.title: Signed dual-square principal symbol and exact owner-conjugation obstruction
create.statement_tex: Fix one orientation of the residual hard-top M2 fixed-a row, put c=nu-tau g/2, n=2|c| and epsilon=sgn(c), and split primitivity by q=du with d|a odd. On any fixed smooth interpolated component whose physical, reciprocal, lift, maximal and owner boundaries are separated from the joint saddle, the k and u dual labels are m=-epsilon ell and d-2h=-epsilon r with ell>0 and r>0 odd; y_*^2=ell/n, k_*^2=n Lambda_(du)/(2ell), b_*=4d^2Xn ell/r^2, and the stationary phase is epsilon(J sqrt(dn ell/r)-sqrt(ar/d)/2)^2. The physical, k and u Gaussian units multiply to e(1/8), and the strict-interior principal coefficient is e(1/8)g^(1/2)b_*^(3/4)[dJ^(1/2)n^(3/4)ell^(1/4)]^(-1) A^circ_(ga,gb_*)(gell/n). The normalized complete physical factor is the centred Fresnel functional, not this point value at collars or endpoints. The scalar frequency map preserves local L2 density. For every literal finite zero-extended integer owner P_E, the exact Fourier stage transports it to F P_E F^(-1), preserving idempotency, rank, norm, complements and one-count; because b_* is generally nonintegral, point evaluation of a sharp owner there is noncanonical. Hence scalar stationary phase and full Hessian rank yield no owner-preserving D-saving. The complete Fresnel transitions, nonlocal owner kernel and signed actual Gram remain open, and the returned denominator row does not meet the accepted terminal M1 range, separability, BV or maximal-owner hypotheses.
create.next_action: Do not repeat the scalar dual-square or determinant route. Attack the literal signed nonzero-shift fixed-a Gram or its conjugated complete-Fresnel owner kernel directly, seeking cancellation across actual q-rows before absolute values. Any stationary reformulation must keep both signs, all transition modules and the exact owner Fourier kernels.
create.reason_for_promotion: The two signed branches, three saddle normalizations, final Gaussian constant, local density identity, nonintegral-saddle interpolation obstruction and exact Fourier conjugation of finite owners are independently reproduced and hostilely scoped. The lemma explicitly does not assert a complete stationary expansion, target-sized remainder, D-saving, polynomial shell or actual lower bound.

reject.reason: For each orientation c=nu-tau g/2 has both signs. With epsilon=sgn(c), the dual phase is epsilon times the square and the labels are m=-epsilon ell, d-2h=-epsilon r.

The point value is only the strict smooth-interior zeroth symbol. Physical collars, reciprocal or maximal endpoints, lift boundaries, hard samples and the collapsing edge require the complete one- or multi-sided Fresnel vector.

Sharp owners are defined on integer q. Different cardinal extensions agree on every primal sample but can differ at the generally nonintegral saddle b_*, with the difference cancelled only by the remaining exact dual integrals.

Square-ray and other sparse prior-owner complements have polynomially many arithmetic jumps and are accepted only in aggregate norms. Their exact Fourier kernels must remain in the transformed vector.
Conjugation preserves projector norm, rank, complements and one-count and inverse Fourier transform returns the original owner. It is an identity, not an estimate.

The denominator scale is dnJ, while b_* couples ell and r inside profiles, maximal support, lifts, collars and owners. The accepted terminal theorem's range, separability, BV and maximal-owner hypotheses fail literally.

Local L2 density is preserved, so scalar square-root capacity remains a factor sqrt(D) above the row target and direct Gram capacity retains the D^2 deficit. Actual directional cancellation is still required.
